title: Canonical planning authority envelope
description: OBJECTIVE: define the daemon-owned versioned payload that can persist the approved-plan and criteria CONTENT together with planning-run evidence instead of today's hash/ref-only PlanProposed body. HARD DEPENDENCY: task-dc21cb4a8f2a4c1c902f3bf3a82a59c2 must be DONE; verify apps/daemon package.json + pnpm-lock importer + a temporary compiled bare @moe/core probe before naming its symbols. DELIVERABLE: one focused apps/daemon planning codec module, exact LF bridge, and test; it seals the existing planning events/gate together with canonical PlanRevision and AcceptanceContract records and checks their server-derived digests against the run submission/criteria bindings. NOT IN SCOPE: changing the HTTP/runtime kind, committing events, approval activation, current readers, or context rendering. VERIFICATION: a focused Vitest invocation for the new test file must print a nonzero count and exit 0.
definitionOfDone: A closed versioned planning-authority envelope contains the canonical PlanRevision and AcceptanceContract bodies plus the existing planning reducer events/gate and the exact project/goal/run/revision bindings needed by later approval.

Admission recomputes both body digests and refuses mismatched submission hash, criteria binding, graph revision, project/goal/run identity, malformed/noncanonical bytes, unsupported version, or extra/accessor fields with exact stable code and layer.
Accepted output and nested records are deeply frozen; the codec has finite item/byte bounds and never reads spec files, NodeMission, review rows, or caller-supplied digest authority.
Tests include one nonempty accepted plan+criteria envelope and a positive-count generated hostile matrix; mutating every cross-binding production check reddens a named exact-code assertion.
The daemon manifest/lock/bare-specifier edge to @moe/core is proved, the focused test prints nonzero counts, and every production source remains <=250 physical lines.

ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS IN THE FIRST GREEN IMPLEMENTATION; both fixed, both now drilled (D20/D21), suite 42 -> 45 tests:
(1) PROXY / DOUBLE-READ. `exactRecord` returned the CALLER's object, and `readBindings` read each member twice (bounds check, then freeze). A Proxy whose `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` trap reports a data descriptor its `get` trap contradicts could pass the bound check and then hand back a different value. Fixed: `isProxy` refusal (mirroring plan-revision-contract.ts) plus a frozen null-prototype SNAPSHOT of the descriptor values, so every member is read exactly once at validation time.
(2) ROSTER SEPARATOR COLLAPSE. The criteria-binding check joined criterion ids with a space, and a criterion id may legally contain a space — so a contract holding the single id "criterion-a criterion-b" satisfied a revision holding ["criterion-a","criterion-b"] and the binding silently passed. Fixed with `JSON.stringify([...ids].sort())` on BOTH sides (injective encoding). New arm: "refuses a criterion roster that only matches once a separator is collapsed".
Honest note: the snapshot half of fix (1) is defence-in-depth and is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT on its own — a non-proxy object cannot change between reads, so `isProxy` is the load-bearing guard and D20 is what kills it. Also checked and found sound: `canonicalText`'s TypeError is unreachable (every admitted leaf is a string), no shared mutable state, no async so no TOCTOU on the byte compare, unknown decode codes fail closed to BYTES_INVALID.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) Sealing raw bytes of the two records instead of admitted bodies — rejected: admission must recompute digests through the published derivations and refuse mismatches; byte-blob sealing would make the envelope a courier, not an authority shape. (b) Local digest implementation — forbidden (no second digest opinion; the core domains are published precisely so consumers compose them). (c) Wiring plan.propose or committing events here — out of scope by the task's own NOT-list; ff82bb75/3544d11c own those. (d) One combined cross-binding drill — rejected: seven independent drills because a combined one passes with a single live check (the 9a1eb61d three-way precedent). (e) Exporting the layer constant for test convenience — rejected: roster churn; assert via the closed type + literal.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: PROBED at claim time (post-63c92f4): (1) dc21cb4a landed — the @moe/core root publishes the full codec surfaces + both derivations (index.ts:116-118/:133-134); the daemon→core edge has two of three legs verified (package.json:23, lock importer present per the scheduler-side pattern — worker re-confirms) with the bare probe as leg three. (2) The surfaces this envelope seals are measured: core planning-run-submission.ts propose/finalize/approvePlan (:110/:140/:172) — approvePlan's input contract IS the binding-field list later approval needs, so the envelope's bindings derive from THAT measurement, not invention; today's PlanProposed body is hash/ref-only (bootstrap-contracts.ts) — the content gap is intact. (3) Daemon planning conventions live in apps/daemon/src/planning/ (planning-services.ts, approval-gate.ts) — style + refusal-shape template. (4) Security-roster discipline: THIS module keeps its layer const module-private (exported closed type) — two exported layer consts already triggered task-120403f7 tonight; do not create a third roster row. (5) Lane state: ff82bb75 and 3544d11c are BLOCKED tonight naming this row — the consumer chain is pre-wired and the completion records both ids (clause 1(a)).
planningNotes.risks: (1) The envelope binding list must come from approvePlan's measured inputs — if the worker finds the approval consumer needs a field this plan did not anticipate (e.g. policy revision), the list follows the measurement and the step note says so. (2) Seven binding drills + three codec drills is the largest drill budget tonight — they are cheap (pure codec, no store) but each must name its distinct arm. (3) The core reducer/gate vocabulary passes through — the two-vocabulary layer assertion (which layer answered) is the rail-6 discipline QA graded hard all night. (4) Pure-codec slice — no store teardown hazards, but the bridge-load child-process check is mandatory (vitest rewrites .js→.ts and hides a broken bridge). (5) Shared worktree: three-file pathspec commit; the planning/ directory is quiet tonight but approval-gate suites are foreign — do not touch.
